findings.text: non-blocking: the setup assertion requires the ambient crew home to hold zero live runs for this node, so any pre-existing stale pointer for the fixture errors all eight cases before the case runs; the done_when asks only that entries be equal before and after, which tolerates a row that was already there. The base arm's eight errors are exactly this assertion firing on r-20261117T093219874690-node-one-worktree, and the head's green depended on that pointer being retired by the coordinator. Comparing the after list against the before list would keep the leak caught without turning external state into a failure of this case.
